failure_class: Muted, disabled and ended tracks are treated as one state
root_invariant: Temporary absence and terminal resource loss are different transitions
proposed_treatment: Derive explicit track states and recovery; avoid reacquiring devices on every transient pause

failure_class: Codec or browser feature assumption has no supported fallback
root_invariant: A capability-dependent operation has a tested availability and failure path
proposed_treatment: Target profiles plus runtime negotiation; no UA-string proof of support

failure_class: Real-time timestamps from different clocks drift or reorder output
root_invariant: Timebase and conversion uncertainty belong to the synchronization contract
proposed_treatment: Type media/device timebases separately; application chooses sync tolerance

failure_class: Code unrelated to a route or interaction ships to the browser
root_invariant: Each shipped artifact has a reachable browser use and explanation
proposed_treatment: Track reachability through captures and imports; measure JS/Wasm plus manifests and HTML

failure_class: Equivalent dependencies or embedded state are duplicated in delivery
root_invariant: Shared semantic identity permits sharing without crossing privacy/version boundaries
proposed_treatment: Deduplicate lawful code/state and measure total cold/warm transfer

failure_class: Independent requests form an accidental waterfall
root_invariant: Dependencies, not source nesting alone, determine required serialization of requests
proposed_treatment: Parallelize only independent authorized work; avoid speculative requests with side effects or privacy cost

failure_class: Per-item data access causes N+1 queries
root_invariant: Set-oriented intent should not accidentally require per-row round trips
proposed_treatment: Derive batching for analyzable queries; instrument foreign-call cardinality and expose unknown plans

failure_class: Data fetching overfetches, underfetches or repeats serialization
root_invariant: Transferred representation contains what the consuming contract needs within policy
proposed_treatment: Project known reads; avoid removing fields required by opaque interop; measure serialization separately

failure_class: Long computation monopolizes the browser main thread
root_invariant: Nonurgent generated work respects interaction scheduling and cancellation
proposed_treatment: Cooperatively schedule or offload eligible computation; profile algorithms whose cost is unknown

failure_class: Critical image/font/resource is discovered too late
root_invariant: Critical content dependencies can be discovered without waiting for irrelevant execution
proposed_treatment: Derive resource discovery from route graph; profile priority and preserve responsive/art-direction choices

failure_class: Offscreen optimization leaves unbounded live DOM or subscriptions
root_invariant: Live object/cardinality budgets are separate from render-work budgets
proposed_treatment: Measure DOM, observers, subscriptions and retained state, not only layout time

failure_class: Query plan or server cold start violates latency assumptions
root_invariant: Compilation validity does not establish deployed cost under actual data and caches
proposed_treatment: Profile cardinality/index/connection/cold-start regimes; choose placement from measured feasible plans

failure_class: Per-key safety hides unbounded distinct-key demand
root_invariant: Aggregate work is bounded across keys, tenants, queues and dependency fanout
proposed_treatment: Compose request, node and tenant budgets with explicit shed/degrade outcomes

failure_class: Retries multiply across independent layers
root_invariant: One logical operation has one composed retry budget
proposed_treatment: Assign retry ownership; account for SDK/proxy retries; respect upstream throttling

failure_class: Same-key clients use identical jitter and synchronize retries
root_invariant: Independent retrying owners must not accidentally share a lockstep schedule
proposed_treatment: Use reproducible seeded entropy with owner/attempt identity; test same-key many-client schedules

failure_class: Recovery releases a backlog faster than dependencies recover
root_invariant: Recovery traffic is admitted within current dependency capacity
proposed_treatment: Budget warmups, queue replay, reconnects and cache regeneration together

failure_class: One tenant exhausts resources needed by others
root_invariant: Tenant isolation includes capacity, not only data visibility
proposed_treatment: Attribute CPU/memory/query/egress costs to tenant and operation; enforce fairness policy

failure_class: Diagnostic or audit pipeline amplifies an outage
root_invariant: Observation work cannot consume unbounded resources or block critical recovery
proposed_treatment: Budget trace queues and attribute cardinality; distinguish best-effort telemetry from required audit

failure_class: Circuit breaker or fallback silently violates correctness
root_invariant: Resilience mechanisms must preserve declared safety or expose unavailability
proposed_treatment: Permit stale fallback only within data/authorization policy; no global magic breaker fallback

failure_class: Valid configuration unexpectedly exceeds safe work or blast radius
root_invariant: Schema validity and operational admission are distinct gates
proposed_treatment: Check semantic limits and rollout scope, then monitor canary outcomes

failure_class: Compatibility checks cover a handler but not its whole durable dependency graph
root_invariant: Every active client, intent, workflow and stored representation has a valid path through deployment
proposed_treatment: Model schemas, operation contracts, policies, keys, workers and retained artifacts together

failure_class: Old assets are deleted while active clients still reference them
root_invariant: Artifact retention is at least the admitted client/version lifetime or has safe recovery
proposed_treatment: Coordinate asset garbage collection with active version policy and draft-preserving reload

failure_class: Rollback restores code but cannot read already-migrated data
root_invariant: Rollback eligibility includes data compatibility and irreversible effects
proposed_treatment: Generate compatibility checks; require explicit irreversible migration/recovery policy

failure_class: Configuration update bypasses code rollout protections
root_invariant: Configuration is executable operational input with a release identity
proposed_treatment: Include configuration in semantic and deployment diffs, canaries and rollback

failure_class: Shared credential or signing-key rotation invalidates all active consumers
root_invariant: Trust material has a lifecycle compatible with active artifact and session lifetimes
proposed_treatment: Track key epochs and overlap; test expiry, emergency revocation and stale clients

failure_class: Distributed failover accepts conflicting authorities
root_invariant: Only an admitted authority epoch may commit where single-writer safety is promised
proposed_treatment: Require host/database guarantees, fence old owners and expose availability loss

failure_class: Migration or background repair is not restartable
root_invariant: Maintenance makes progress through recoverable, versioned checkpoints
proposed_treatment: Generate checkpoint and restart protocol; retain explicit data conversion and error handling

failure_class: Source contract differs from the exact deployed artifact
root_invariant: Admission depends on actual artifact requirements, not only claimed manifest
proposed_treatment: Retain actual import/component-type checks and bind contract to artifact digest

failure_class: Trusted dependency acquires unneeded runtime authority
root_invariant: Dependency authority is the granted minimum, not the importing app's whole environment
proposed_treatment: Propagate per-package requirements; isolate untrusted code where host boundaries actually enforce them

failure_class: Build plugin compromise bypasses runtime sandbox claims
root_invariant: The compiler/build chain is a separate privileged trust boundary
proposed_treatment: Restrict build network/secrets/files; verify source-to-artifact provenance separately

failure_class: Authentic artifact is mistaken for benign code
root_invariant: Identity and provenance do not establish acceptable behavior
proposed_treatment: Keep provenance, vulnerability review and permission admission separate

failure_class: Undeclared environment input changes build result
root_invariant: Build outputs depend only on declared, identified inputs
proposed_treatment: Track environment, locale, filesystem, toolchains and generated resources; reject undeclared access

failure_class: Incremental result differs from a clean build
root_invariant: Incremental computation is observationally equivalent to fresh computation
proposed_treatment: Key by complete semantic inputs; compare incremental/clean outputs under edits and cache corruption

failure_class: Package or declaration identity collapses distinct versions or sources
root_invariant: Equal spelling does not establish package/declaration identity across build or ABI
proposed_treatment: Include authoritative package provenance and version semantics; never use final name segments as identity

failure_class: Pinned dependency cannot be obtained or reproduced
root_invariant: Reproducibility includes recoverable inputs, not merely a lockfile
proposed_treatment: Retain licensed build inputs and verify integrity; declare offline/recovery support

failure_class: Generated source maps or diagnostics expose secret source content
root_invariant: Debug metadata obeys the same audience boundary as executable output
proposed_treatment: Partition source maps, diagnostics and build logs by audience; audit public release contents

failure_class: Application-only validation loses a race or is bypassed by another writer
root_invariant: Persistent invariants are enforced at the authoritative write boundary
proposed_treatment: Derive supported constraints from domain authority; explicitly map external database invariants

failure_class: Database backend changes semantics of null, constraint or transaction behavior
root_invariant: Adapters must preserve requested semantic guarantees or reject unsupported mapping
proposed_treatment: Conformance-test backend semantics rather than treating SQL dialects as equivalent

failure_class: Transaction holds scarce locks while waiting on unrelated remote work
root_invariant: Transaction lifetime is bounded and external effects do not silently extend critical sections
proposed_treatment: Detect unsupported remote awaits and budget transaction time; require explicit justified pattern

failure_class: Deadlock or serialization retry repeats unsafe side effects
root_invariant: A retried transaction body is replay-safe at every external effect
proposed_treatment: Keep external effects behind post-commit protocol; surface bounded conflict retry

failure_class: Backup exists but cannot restore the promised state
root_invariant: Recoverability is demonstrated by restore and reconciliation, not backup-job success
proposed_treatment: Test backups, keys, schema and operation ledger together; report actual recovery limits

failure_class: Destructive maintenance executes under ordinary application authority
root_invariant: Irreversible broad actions require narrowly scoped maintenance authority and target identity
proposed_treatment: Distinguish read/write from destructive maintenance; confirm target/environment in deploy plan

failure_class: Database record and external blob have inconsistent lifecycle
root_invariant: Cross-store referential lifecycle needs staged publication and recoverable cleanup
proposed_treatment: Model pending upload, committed reference and orphan reclamation; no fake cross-store atomicity

failure_class: Metric schema is correct but records the wrong business event
root_invariant: A metric identifies its event, unit, population and observation point
proposed_treatment: Separate assigned, exposed, activated and completed events; derive mechanical fields only

failure_class: Experiment assignment and delivered treatment disagree
root_invariant: Assignment, eligibility, delivery and exposure are distinct recorded facts
proposed_treatment: Carry assignment identity through cache/placement; log actual exposure under consent policy

failure_class: Sampling or missing data is presented as a full count
root_invariant: Measurement coverage and sampling semantics remain attached to aggregates
proposed_treatment: Expose sample weights, dropped-event counters and completeness; do not infer business absence

failure_class: Trace explains local execution but loses cross-boundary cause
root_invariant: Every claimed causal edge corresponds to propagated identity/evidence
proposed_treatment: Propagate operation/attempt/resource/commit IDs through generated adapters; distinguish cause from correlation

failure_class: Feature flag changes authority or cache meaning without review
root_invariant: Behavioral configuration changes are semantic deployment changes
proposed_treatment: Include flag-enabled effects, policy and key dependencies in semantic diffs; no hidden privileged bypass

failure_class: Replay records too little to reproduce or too much private data
root_invariant: Replay claims state which inputs are captured, redacted, substituted or unavailable
proposed_treatment: Record scheduler/clock/random/foreign outcomes where allowed; mark opaque/redacted segments nonreplayable

failure_class: Audit durability is confused with best-effort analytics delivery
root_invariant: Each observation stream declares whether loss is acceptable
proposed_treatment: Separate transactional audit from operational trace and analytics; budgets must not silently drop mandatory records

failure_class: A witness fails for a different defect than its claimed invariant
root_invariant: A negative witness's prerequisites are valid and only the intended defect differs from its control
proposed_treatment: Operationalize existing witness rule after value typing; check all prerequisites and causal evidence

failure_class: Passing test is vacuous or discards the relevant outcome
root_invariant: The observation would fail when the promised behavior is removed
proposed_treatment: Check actual outcomes under forced schedules; mutate cancellation/publication/decoding independently

failure_class: A stand-in implements missing semantics and makes the demo pass
root_invariant: End-to-end evidence traverses the generated production path it claims
proposed_treatment: Require source-to-artifact-to-host-to-browser reachability for integrated claims

failure_class: Test oracle is derived from the same incorrect implementation
root_invariant: Single semantic authority does not eliminate independent evidence
proposed_treatment: Derive routine fixtures but retain independent standards/model oracles and adversarial inputs

failure_class: Browser automation is mistaken for complete device/AT compatibility
root_invariant: Compatibility claims are bounded by actual browser, device and assistive technology coverage
proposed_treatment: Test real mobile lifecycle, keyboard, screen readers and browser policies; record exact matrix

failure_class: Hot reload preserves state whose meaning changed
root_invariant: HMR state preservation requires semantic compatibility, otherwise explicit reset/migration
proposed_treatment: Compare state shape, identity, capabilities and active resources; preserve only valid state

failure_class: Diagnostic points to generated machinery instead of the semantic cause
root_invariant: Every inferred conclusion can explain its originating facts and violated boundary
proposed_treatment: Preserve source spans through transformations; show shortest causal chain and legal repair

failure_class: Rename or incremental refactor changes semantic identity accidentally
root_invariant: Refactoring preserves denotation unless an intentional public contract change is declared
proposed_treatment: Test rename/module reorder equivalence; report actual API-identity changes separately

failure_class: Build or optimization succeeds without preserving source semantics
root_invariant: Target validity is not semantic equivalence to the checked source
proposed_treatment: Compare typed IR and emitted behavior on adversarial programs; audit information-losing projections

failure_class: Foreign type declaration is treated as proof of foreign runtime values
root_invariant: External values and behavior enter only through validated contracts
proposed_treatment: No TypeScript assertion import as trusted value; decode and constrain effects

failure_class: Two independently authored interfaces compete as one API authority
root_invariant: Each interface has one authoritative schema; projections cannot re-declare it
proposed_treatment: Pleris-owned API emits bindings; foreign-owned API imports schema; semantic wrapper adds distinct domain meaning

failure_class: Component/core ABI equality erases important semantic distinctions
root_invariant: Each boundary checks the richest contract necessary before lowering loses information
proposed_treatment: Audit semantic type, component signature and core encoding as different relations

failure_class: Embedded island and host both own the same state or DOM
root_invariant: Interop names the authority for state, navigation, DOM and lifecycle
proposed_treatment: One direction per state authority; bridge typed events and scoped resources

failure_class: Transport schema is confused with full API behavior
root_invariant: An adapter contract covers behavior as well as data shape
proposed_treatment: Model REST/GraphQL/RPC errors, pagination, retries, ordering and auth; browser gRPC uses a compatible transport adapter

failure_class: Foreign widget receives implicit whole-page authority
root_invariant: Interop guarantees depend on enforceable origin/realm/host confinement
proposed_treatment: Expose narrow node, data and effect interfaces; use real isolation for hostile code

failure_class: Coding agent changes its own evidence or grants to make failure disappear
root_invariant: Verification and authority approval are outside the mutation authority of the evaluated patch
proposed_treatment: Separate agent-writable source from trusted evaluation and grant approval; semantic diff highlights weakened guarantees

failure_class: Hallucinated package/API becomes an unsafe dependency acquisition
root_invariant: Unresolved external names cannot silently create trusted dependency authority
proposed_treatment: Require existing typed exports and explicit dependency/capability review; package existence alone is insufficient

failure_class: Safety feature rejects legitimate applications or overwhelms authors
root_invariant: A conservative rule must preserve an acceptable supported-program envelope
proposed_treatment: Maintain positive counterexamples and task-based readability tests; move dynamic cases to checked boundaries

failure_class: Automatic placement is legal but surprising or operationally unstable
root_invariant: Optimization preferences are subordinate to constraints and reviewable plan stability
proposed_treatment: Separate feasibility from cost optimization; explain and diff plan changes; profile before migration

failure_class: Valid program implements the wrong product requirement
root_invariant: Structural safety is not a proof that the chosen policy or requirement is right
proposed_treatment: Expose assumptions and domain policy changes; never score compile success as product success

failure_class: Browser or infrastructure exploit bypasses the platform's trusted base
root_invariant: Guarantees are conditional on the integrity of the named trusted computing base
proposed_treatment: Document compiler/runtime/host/browser trust assumptions and remediation; no language-level universal immunity
